input: Write a due diligence memo on Canva

red_flags.claim: AI unit economics: Fortune reported that unexpectedly high AI delivery costs prompted slower product rollout and a reduction in expected revenue growth from 30% to 20%. These were forecasts, not actual results.

Execution disruption: the company’s restructuring announcement, observed as of this date, says 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. This is an impact count, not a verified count of completed layoffs.

Valuation pressure: investor marks reported in September 2026 ranged from US$34.9 billion to US$39.3 billion, below the US$42 billion employee share-sale valuation announced in August 2025. These marks are not new financing prices.

Reporting controls: ASIC reports that Canva Pty Ltd paid A$198,000 for alleged late financial-report lodgment; its FY2024 consolidated report was lodged on 2026-03-27, after the 2025-04-30 deadline. Payment was not an admission of liability.

Third-party security exposure: Canva’s notification published by Turkey’s regulator described a breach affecting data associated with 424 Turkish organizations; the affected individual count remained unknown at notification.

Product-specific patent exposure: the Delhi High Court dismissed Canva’s appeal against interim restrictions on its Present and Record feature in India. The ruling was preliminary, not a final infringement judgment.

traction.claim: Company claim for 2025, reported by TechCrunch: more than 265 million monthly active users, over 31 million paid users, and 20% growth in monthly active users.
Company claim for 2025: B2B business, defined as companies with more than 25 seats, grew 100% and reached $500 million in annual recurring revenue.

Company claim, observed as of this date: Canva’s business page names Zoom, Salesforce, Skyscanner, F45 and OMD in customer case-study results. These are company-selected references, not independently verified customer-contract disclosures.

Company claim: its ChatGPT integration had generated more than 26 million user conversations by October 2025. TechCrunch also reported integrations with ChatGPT and Claude; commercial partnership terms were not disclosed.

missing_fields: Latest audited consolidated financial statements; current net income, EBITDA, cash, debt, cash runway and AI contribution margins.
Exact post-restructuring headcount and the split between eliminated, relocated and otherwise changed roles.
Independently current CFO incumbency and CTO successor as of 2026-11-09.
Complete primary-financing history after the verified 2021 round, current capitalization table, and proceeds or completion details of the announced 2025 employee share sale.
Company-specific sanctions and beneficial-owner screening results; no sanctions clearance is asserted.
Primary court confirmation of the reported US patent-case dismissal and any later merits disposition of the Indian patent dispute.
A representative quantitative employee-review trend; the available employee comments are anecdotal.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: ASIC record observed as of this date: Canva Pty Ltd and three named group affiliates each paid A$198,000, totaling A$792,000, over alleged failure to lodge FY2024 financial reports by 2025-04-30. Canva Pty Ltd lodged the consolidated report on 2026-03-27. ASIC states payment is neither an admission of liability nor a conviction.

Turkey’s KVKK published Canva Pty Ltd’s breach notification describing unauthorized access involving a third-party tool and suspected data exfiltration. Data associated with 424 Turkish organizations was affected; individual numbers were unknown. Exposed categories included employee business-contact details and certain customer documents. The regulator’s examination was ongoing at publication.

In Canva v. RxPrism, the Delhi High Court dismissed Canva’s appeal, leaving interim restrictions on Present and Record in India in place in the dispute over patent IN360726. The court expressly confined its observations to the preliminary stage; merits remained for trial.
DigiMedia Tech filed a patent-infringement complaint against Canva Pty Ltd in the Eastern District of Texas. The complaint contains allegations and requests for relief, not findings of infringement.

Aggregator-reported disposition: Patsnap records DigiMedia Tech v. Canva Pty Ltd, case 2:25-cv-00808, as closed with prejudice on this date following the parties’ stipulation, with each side bearing its own costs and fees. The underlying dismissal order was not independently verified.

reputation.claim: Trustpilot review-aggregator snapshot: 4.0/5 across 8,093 reviews, with 51% five-star and 29% one-star ratings. Displayed comments include a cancellation/refund complaint alongside praise for video editing, presentations and usability. These are self-selected customer reports, not adjudicated findings.

Glassdoor employee-review snapshot is mixed: January and July 2026 examples praise compensation, while January examples criticize communication, promotion assessments and leadership clarity. These individual reviews do not establish a representative company-wide trend.
Critical press: Fortune focused on AI delivery costs forcing slower rollout and a reduced growth forecast, challenging the economics of Canva’s expansion into broader workplace software.

output.verdict: Canva shows substantial company-reported subscription scale, paid adoption and named enterprise deployments, with its founding team still listed in senior operating roles. Before investing, reconcile revenue with audited accounts and examine AI unit economics, investor valuation markdowns, restructuring execution, reporting controls, breach remediation and the Indian patent restrictions.

financial_signals.claim: Company claim in its 2025 annual review: revenue reached $3.5 billion. This is a company statement, not independently verified audited financial information; the cited revenue sentence does not expressly identify the dollar currency.

Company claim reported by TechCrunch: annual recurring revenue reached $4 billion by the end of 2025. This is ARR, not recognized annual revenue, and should not be substituted for the annual-review revenue figure.

Fortune reported that Canva reduced expected revenue growth from 30% to 20% as higher-than-expected AI costs slowed rollout. CEO Melanie Perkins said the company was rebuilding architecture, reducing unit costs and strengthening the business model. The growth figures were forecasts.

Company claim, announcement observed as of this date: restructuring will impact 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, and include employee departures. Perkins said growth had slowed for the first time in a decade. Exact completed layoffs and resulting headcount were not established.

team.claim: The official leadership page, observed as of this date, lists co-founders Melanie Perkins as CEO, Cliff Obrecht as COO and Cameron Adams as CPO. It also lists Zach Kitschke as chief marketing officer and Jennie Rogerson as global head of people.

EdTech Innovation Hub reported CTO Brendan Humphreys’ announced departure, scheduled for 2026-06-19, with a subsequent advisory role. It reported prior experience at Atlassian and as founder of Cenqua. Completion of the departure and a successor were not independently reconfirmed.

The Australian Financial Review reported that four senior leaders were leaving during May 2026. Its accessible reporting named growth lead Iain Dowling, who announced his resignation, and senior engineering director Jonathan Ross, scheduled to leave at month-end.

business.claim: Canva is an Australian technology company operating a globally used online design and content-creation platform. Its business offering supports visual communication, collaboration and content production.

Pricing page observed as of this date: freemium subscription model spanning Free and paid Pro plans for individuals, Business for individuals and teams, and sales-led Enterprise for organizations. Education offerings cover eligible schools, educators and students.

funding.claim: Company announcement: a US$200 million funding round led by T. Rowe Price valued Canva at US$40 billion.

Reuters reported an announced employee share sale at a US$42 billion valuation, led by existing shareholder Fidelity Management, with JPMorgan’s asset-management division joining as a new investor. This was employee secondary liquidity, not a disclosed primary cash raise; transaction size was not revealed.

Investor valuation estimates reported by Forbes Australia: T. Rowe Price implied US$38.2 billion, Franklin Templeton US$39.3 billion during the June 2026 quarter, and Blackbird US$34.9 billion. These are investor marks, distinct from the announced US$42 billion secondary-sale valuation.
